DEFINITION · qeva:1:metric-space@1

Metric space

A metric assigns a distance satisfying nonnegativity, identity, symmetry, and the triangle inequality.

editorialanalysis · geometry · topology

PLAIN

The idea

A metric assigns a distance satisfying nonnegativity, identity, symmetry, and the triangle inequality.

EXACT

The compact statement

A metric d:X×X→ℝ≥0 obeys d(x,y)=0 iff x=y, d(x,y)=d(y,x), and d(x,z)≤d(x,y)+d(y,z).

EXAMPLE

Absolute difference |x−y| is a metric on ℝ.

BOUNDARY / CAVEAT

Many useful topologies are not generated by a metric.

ASSUMPTIONS

  • The declared metric geometry context is fixed.
